rooms.title: Ninety Seconds
rooms.setting: Night shift, 21:04. A step-down room. The 21:00 meds are due.

beats.text: The nurse scans the patient's wristband and the antibiotic.
While the scanner beeps, she notices his words are coming a half-beat slower than they did at 19:00.
She frees the oxygen tubing kinked under his arm.
His daughter's hands are shaking. The nurse asks if she's eaten today. She hasn't.
She hangs the antibiotic, checks the IV site and leaves.

rooms.prompt: What did the nurse just do?

A.label: Gave a medication
A.outcome: Yes. That's the part the chart shows: one barcode scan at 21:04.

B.label: Assessed his neuro status
B.outcome: Yes. She caught a subtle change. No field was opened. It lives only in her head until it gets worse.

C.label: Cared for his family
C.outcome: Yes. She noticed the daughter hadn't eaten. There's nowhere to chart that.

rooms.reveal: All three. The record shows one.

rooms.setting: 03:10. A patient recovering from abdominal surgery. The nurse has four other patients.

beats.text: His breathing is faster and shallower than an hour ago. He's using his shoulders to breathe.
His SpO2 still reads 94%. Nothing has alarmed.
She raises the head of the bed, splints his incision with a pillow and coaches him through slow breaths.

rooms.prompt: It's 03:15. Four other patients. What does she do?

A.label: Stay with him
A.outcome: By 03:25 he's settled. At 05:45 she charts routine vitals: RR 20, SpO2 95%. Fifteen minutes at the bedside left no trace.

B.label: Chart it now
B.outcome: The record gets an accurate entry at 03:16. He gets four fewer minutes of her coaching. The chart improved. Did the care?

C.label: Call a rapid response
C.outcome: The team arrives at 03:22. He's already better. The record shows a rapid response call, not the nursing that came before it.

rooms.reveal: Every path is good care. Each leaves a different trace, or none.

rooms.title: He's Not Himself

beats.text: He knows his name, where he is, the date and why he's here.
His wife pulls the nurse aside: "He's not himself today. He'd never be this quiet."
His vitals are in normal range. The nurse opens the flowsheet.

rooms.prompt: Which box captures what his wife just said?

A.label: Neuro: Alert & oriented x4 ☑
A.outcome: True. And it says he's fine.

B.label: Behavior: Calm, cooperative ☑
B.outcome: Also true. It records his quiet as a good thing.

C.label: Family concern: free-text comment
C.outcome: Closest. But free text is often the part structured reports and models skip.

rooms.reveal: 20:40: his heart rate and temperature climb, and the sepsis alert fires. The earliest signal was his wife's sentence, six hours before.
rooms.gestureLink: Use the Phase 7 'chart it' compression on the chosen box, so the wife's sentence visibly flattens into the checkbox.

rooms.title: Third Night
rooms.setting: Comfort care. The nurse's third night in a row with this patient.

beats.text: His breathing has slowed to 8, with long pauses. His knees are mottled.
On her first night, she learned he settles when she hums the hymn his late wife used to sing. She hums it now. His face softens.
His son is 10 minutes away. She asks the resident to hold the family call until he arrives, so he can hear it in the room.

rooms.prompt: Which of these can she chart?

A.label: RR 8 with apneic pauses, mottled knees
A.outcome: There's a field for that. Empirical knowing, recorded.

B.label: He settles to his wife's hymn
B.outcome: No field. Personal and aesthetic knowing becomes dark matter.

C.label: She held the call for his son
C.outcome: No field. Ethical knowing becomes dark matter.

rooms.reveal: Only one kind of knowing has a home in the record. Unchosen options drift into the dark matter layer.
